# <First name>

Mohammad

## Study background

M.Sc. Computer Science, 1st semester

## Interests

Full-stack development, Gaming

## Fun fact

I’ll patiently sit through a 40-hour story-driven game with zero skips, but waiting 30 seconds for a build pipeline to finish tests my entire sanity.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today

AI is unmatched for ripping through boilerplate and syntax lookups, but it frequently hallucinates subtle logical flaws that make debugging twice as tedious. It speeds up the typing part of programming without genuinely understanding system architecture or context. Right now, it works best as an eager junior developer whose every commit needs thorough code review.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years

The core job will shift almost entirely from typing code to specifying requirements, edge cases, and architectural constraints. Writing raw boilerplate by hand will largely disappear, replaced by autonomous agents managed by engineers acting as system architects. True engineering value will center on verification, fault tolerance, and knowing what to build rather than how to type it out.

## My hot take on AI

AI doesn’t make bad developers good; it just helps them generate catastrophic technical debt at record speed.


=== Nithya.md ===
# Nithya

## Study background

M.Sc. Computer Science, 7th semester (Thesis stage)

## Interests

Distributed Systems, Cloud Architecture, Badminton, Board games

## Fun fact

I have rewritten my thesis abstract more times than I have recompiled my actual code.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today

AI assistants are fantastic productivity multipliers for well-understood domains and boilerplate generation, but they break down when faced with complex legacy enterprise codebases. They often exhibit blind confidence on subtle synchronization primitives and concurrency issues. Right now, AI acts as a fast copilot, but you cannot let it navigate without senior oversight.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years

Engineering will center heavily on systems integration, prompt-driven formal verification, and distributed consensus rather than mundane feature programming. Junior roles will evolve into system orchestration positions where knowing failure modes and domain invariants will matter far more than knowing low-level library APIs.

## My hot take on AI

AI autocomplete hasn't eliminated bugs; it has just made them compile much faster.
